To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetic ablation IL-10 in mice significantly heightens sensitivity tumor growth and metastasis.
endogenous IL10 inhibits tumor growth by limiting the development of myeloid derived suppressor cells and regulatory T cells, two key components in the immunosupressive tumor microenvironment.
IL-10(-) mice are more sensitive to tumor development, growth and metastasis, which was associated with an increase in MDSC and Treg cells, which in turn were induced by IL-10(-)-MDSCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunobiology of IL-10 and its role in the regulation of immune responses and tumor growth.
a better understanding of the mechanisms of tumor growth and metastasis.
the mechanisms that underlie immune suppression in the tumor environment and the role of IL-10 as an important regulator of these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of IL-10 on tumor growth and progression is dependent on the tumor model and the tumor stage.
IL-10 is a tumor suppressive cytokine.
IL-10 ablation enhances the immunogenic potential of tumors and that IL-10 is a tumor-promoting cytokine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-10 is an anti-inflammatory cytokine, and that its absence promotes tumor development, and that IL-1 signaling is a major pathway by which IL-10 deficiency promotes tumor growth and angiogenesis.
IL-10 deficiency promotes tumor development by increasing MDSCs and Treg cell numbers and function in the tumor microenvironment.
endogenous IL10 promotes tumor growth through the induction of myeloid derived suppressor cells (MDS) and regulatory T (T) cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 in tumor growth is more complex than previously thought, and it may not be a general tumor-promoting cytokine as previously believed.
IL-10 is not a protumor cytokine.

IL-10 is an important tumor suppressor cytokine that inhibits the development of immunosuppressive cells in the tumor microenvironment, and thus, it should be considered for therapeutic targeting in cancer.
